newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: "I'm no Evita," says Peronists' election hopeful.
newsitem.headline: "I'm no Evita," says Peronists' election hopeful.

text.p: Hilda Duhalde, the Peronist Party's choice to fight key elections in the Argentine Congress in October, has kicked off her campaign by rejecting comparisons with the much-adored, late Eva Peron.
"I absolutely reject all comparisons with Evita, because she was unique and unrepeatable," Duhalde, the wife of Peronist Gov. Eduardo Duhalde, said on local television late on Tuesday.

Hilda Duhalde, known to most Argentines as "Chiche" or simply "La senora", has a huge following in her husband's Buenos Aires Province, where an army of 17,000 women volunteers hand out milk and food to 600,000 poor every day.

Her charity work, helped by a budget from the province of $280 million, triggers comparisons with Evita, though Duhalde has shown none of the glamour or charisma that still inspires mystical devotion to Evita in many Argentines.

Evita, the poor girl turned radio starlet who became the glamorous second wife of Juan Peron, was revered as a saintly champion of the poor, who she always called her beloved "descamisados" (shirtless ones). Evita died of cancer in 1952 at age 33, plunging Argentina into mourning.

Beginning her congressional campaign as top of the ruling Peronists' list of candidates for deputy of the huge province -- home to no less than 40 percent of Argentina's voters -- Duhalde told supporters on Tuesday:
"If I become a legislator, I will work in parliament on the only issue I know, which is social problems. I have a lot to learn but I know what my job is -- the people's problems."

October's mid-term elections will be the first battle of the 1999 presidential contest and Chiche Duhalde's success is the key to her husband's campaign to succeed President Carlos Menem. So far, he is the leading candidate for the job.
Political analyst Rosendo Fraga said Menem's insistence on Duhalde running for office was "a clever strategy. She is based on the Evita model, I would say she's the closest thing we have seen."

"It's very well for Mrs. Duhalde to join the political contest, but the people, and most of all the Peronists, must see she is not Evita's successor, but more like the heir of the (upper class) Ladies of Charity," said Melchor Posse, second-in-command of the opposition Radical Party.
